summary: Both Jan occurrences are already represented in the entry. Jan 1.50/2439 matches the inherited QM 2461 qaliyat/meat/salting/containers passage; Jan 1.50/2442 is textually identical to the QM 2464 ksido question. These are concordance observations, not proof that either legacy QM number is wrong.

The active I Infectum-wa has a human agent and meat object; ksido is the resulting meat property in the existing Part. Pass. box. The sequential salting verb mmalḥiwole does not by itself settle whether kəsdiwo is salting, broader preservation or an earlier preparation stage. Existing German gloss and cautious English pickle (?) are preserved.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation. Analyses rest on the Turoyo; any English quoted below is copied from that supplied translation.

Ask a native speaker which preparation stage kəsdiwo denotes before mmalḥiwole at Jan 1.50/2439: curing/preserving broadly, salting itself or cutting/preparation? The supplied evidence does not justify changing einsalzen, einpökeln.
Confirm the concordance QM 2461 = Jan 1.50/2439 and QM 2464 = Jan 1.50/2442 before enriching citation metadata.
